gloss: New Year's greeting; Happy New Year

definitions.gloss: New Year's greeting; Happy New Year
definitions.explanation: A formal expression used on New Year's cards and decorations to celebrate the new year. Literally means 'celebrating the new year.' Primarily a written greeting.

examples.japanese: {年賀状|ねんがじょう}に「{賀正|がしょう}」と{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote 'Happy New Year' on the New Year's card.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{入|い}り{口|ぐち}に「{賀正|がしょう}」の{飾|かざ}りが{出|で}ていた。
examples.english: A New Year's decoration saying 'Happy New Year' was displayed at the company entrance.

examples.japanese: 「{賀正|がしょう}」は{目上|めうえ}の{人|ひと}への{年賀状|ねんがじょう}には{使|つか}わない{方|ほう}がいい。
examples.english: It's better not to use 'gashou' on New Year's cards to people of higher status.

notes:
USAGE:
{賀正|がしょう} is a two-character New Year's greeting commonly printed on {年賀状|ねんがじょう} (New Year's cards) and seasonal decorations. It is considered a somewhat casual abbreviated form.

IMPORTANT: Two-character greetings like {賀正|がしょう} are traditionally seen as abbreviated and therefore less formal. When writing to superiors or elders, four-character greetings such as {謹賀新年|きんがしんねん} are preferred.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {賀正|がしょう}の{飾|かざ}り (New Year's greeting decoration)
- {年賀状|ねんがじょう}に{賀正|がしょう}と{書|か}く (write 'gashou' on a New Year's card)

RELATED WORDS:
- {謹賀新年|きんがしんねん}: respectful New Year's greeting (formal, four characters)
- {迎春|げいしゅん}: welcoming the new year
- {年賀状|ねんがじょう}: New Year's postcard
